question: A 40 m stretch of roadside on one side of a driving aisle is available for parking spaces. Each space is 2.5 m wide (the perpendicular distance between adjacent marking lines). Each perpendicular parking space occupies 2.5 m along the roadside; the marking lines of angled parking spaces form an acute angle of \(30^\circ\) with the driving aisle. What is the maximum number of perpendicular spaces and angled spaces, respectively? (Answer in order, separated by a comma.)
solution: Perpendicular parking: \(40\div2.5=16\) spaces. Each angled space occupies \(2.5\div\sin30^\circ=5\) m along the roadside, giving \(40\div5=8\) spaces.

solutionMethods.explanation:
For angled parking, let \(A\) and \(B\) be where adjacent marking lines meet the roadside. Drop a perpendicular from \(B\) to the marking line through \(A\), extending it if necessary, and call the foot \(C\). Then \(\triangle ABC\) is right-angled at \(C\), \(\angle BAC=30^\circ\), and \(BC=2.5\) m.

The side opposite \(30^\circ\) is half the hypotenuse, so each angled space occupies \(AB=2\times2.5=5\) m along the roadside. Thus \(40\div5=8\) angled spaces fit. Perpendicular spaces give \(40\div2.5=16\) spaces. Both counts use all 40 m, so an additional space cannot fit. The answer is \(16,8\).
solutionMethods.label: Use the 30-degree right-triangle property
